title: Clipped-Gaussian bias: PPO trains on the raw sample while the plant sees the clipped one
label: inferred
what: KNOWN_ISSUES 'What is real' paragraph: PPO stores the raw action and its log_prob while the environment responds to the clipped one.
result: [inferred] 'With 68% of components saturated, most of the policy's output distribution sits where moving the mean further changes the plant not at all -- the standard bias from sampling an unbounded Gaussian into a bounded action space.' Later narrowed for the tail habit: the options study ranked the clipped Gaussian's dead zone 'at most a contributor beyond a mean of about 1.2' (reward slope past +1 cut only 1.34-1.94x at means 1.05-1.11, open loop, noise on tail_3 only), and P1 (which removed most of the training-row dead zone) did not remove the pin. || [also, S31] dE[clip a]/dmu cut about 4x at mu 1.11 (0.22-0.27), but the expected reward slope is cut far less (1.3-1.9x at 1.05-1.11). Measured pinned means 1.01-1.11 keep about half or more of the restoring slope. P1 removed the dead zone from training rows and the pin stayed. Ranked: at most a contributor beyond mu about 1.2.

title: Posture tests verified; the posture pathway and the positive loop came after the tail rise began, and s60 has the opposite pitch sensitivity
label: measured
what: An adversarial verifier with its own code (nothing imported): test 1 from the records with noise-matched departures (k = 2/3/5 SD), a short-window hinge and a 400-resample block bootstrap; tests 2-3 on its own settled states (seeds 5001-5010, 26 policies) with its own sweep (local derivative and 0-6 deg fit), illusion and plant arms; added probes of the r10 F2 checkpoints s42/s80 at 1,048,576 and 2,097,152 (local, never probed by the tests) and of s60 at 1.05-8.39M.
result: [measured, VPOST NOTES l10-31, l209-230] Test 1's negative answer holds and gets stronger; tests 2-3 reproduce closely (corrections in L161-L163). M1: at 1,048,576 the s42 network had no nose-down-to-tail pathway (+0.005 per deg), a negative loop (G -0.250) and c0 -0.06; at 2,097,152 (early rise, c0 +0.238) the pathway was -0.020 (about 1/8 of its 3,145,728 value), G -0.386, s80 transplant -0.058 (control -0.002); at 3,145,728 pathway -0.093, G 0.261, c0 0.411. So the pathway and the positive loop grew after the tail began rising (between 2.1M and 3.15M); they amplify the habit at 3.15M and later, not where it started. Deterministic play at 1,048,576: s42 -0.27 against s80 -0.75 deg. M2: s60 pitch slope per deg nose-up +0.013 (1.05M), +0.085 (5.24M), +0.045 (6.29M), +0.027 (7.34M), +0.005 (8.39M); G -0.47 -> -0.27 -> -0.11 -> +0.23 -> +0.32; c0 +0.02 -> +0.61: offset growth plus a loop turning positive is common to both habits, the nose-down pathway is specific to s42 (correlational, one run). M3: at a fixed observation (the bank's statue_settled row) the s42 tail command rose at 1.3-1.6M (-0.11 at 1.05M -> +0.08 at 1.57M, VPOST F11 l131; PTIME bank_drive.txt's 262,144-step bin medians are -0.105 at 1.049M and +0.030 at 1.573M, first sustained +0.05 above the reference at 1,409,024, l8-l10, l28), ahead of the pitch: the first rise was a posture-independent change in the policy [inferred]; the bank reads through each checkpoint's own normaliser, so the drift is not separated there. M4: test 1's timing claims are threshold-dependent. M5: the closed-loop tail -> posture coupling is missing from test 2's arithmetic. M6: G's definition matters for s80 (local -0.72 against fit -0.28); the closed-loop rail share depends on the seed sample (0.82 against 0.67). M7: not checked: every r9 claim, the start-checkpoint clamp (F10), the gravity-only arm, the 20 s check and the static plant (T3-3). F12: the tests' coverage list omitted that the 1.05M and 2.10M checkpoints were local.

title: H-POSTURE: a body positioning drives the tail habit (narrowed: a learned amplifier in the s42 lineage from mid-rise on; not a mechanical push and not the origin)
label: inferred
what: The maintainer's question of 19:55 UTC (L160), tested three ways: timing in the records (L161), the policies' response to posture inputs (L162) and the plant in the held postures (L163), with an adversarial verifier (L164).
result: [inferred, from the verified results of L161-L164] Ruled out: a mechanical push (the plant's tail map and tail-up cost are the same in every posture, L163) and a posture shift that comes first and pulls the tail up (in r10 s42 the tail bias rose first, at about 1.20M, and at a fixed observation it was rising by 1.3-1.6M; nose-down followed about 0.17M later; the same shifts occur without a rail; L161, L164). Supported within its scope: in the s42 lineage from 3,145,728 (mid-rise) on, the networks map the perceived nose-down pitch (gravity and prey direction in pelvis coordinates) and the lineage's leg angles to the tail offset that the learned loop amplifies to the bound (L162). The pathway and the positive loop grew after the rise began (absent at 1,048,576; about 1/8 at 2,097,152), so the posture is an amplifier of a habit already under way, not its origin (VPOST T2-7, M1). Specific to s42: s60 parked with the opposite pitch sensitivity (M2). Not testable without training: whether training built the pathway because of the posture, or the two grew together (PPOL NOTES l56-61). Unchecked: the r9 claims, F8, F10, the gravity-only arm, the 20 s check, T3-3.

title: Technical lessons from the normaliser probe and the posture tests
label: inferred
what: What this record draws from L157-L165 (§6.1 items 14-15).
result: [inferred, from the measured L157-L164] (14) A drifting normaliser is a record before it is a cause: the tail_3 statistics drifted because the tail rose, and at fixed weights the drift lowered the gain; separate drift from weights by statistics swaps and layer grafts before blaming the normaliser; its influence on training needs a frozen-statistics continuation. (15) A posture can feed a habit through what the policy sees, not through the body: the plant is the same in every posture, while the s42 networks read pitch and leg angles as a tail offset; and what amplifies a habit late need not be where it began (the pathway and the positive loop grew after the rise; s60 has the opposite sensitivity). Test the plant and the network separately, at checkpoints before the rise and in more than one lineage.
